title: A Multi-Clause Ending: Sequencing Meets Result

sections.title: Putting the whole toolkit to work at once
sections.content: A satisfying ending often needs more than one connector working together: a *miután* or *mielőtt* clause to place the last event in time, then *végül* or *az eredmény az volt, hogy* to say what it amounted to. Two new closing words round out the set: *tanulság* ("the moral, the lesson learned") and *kudarc* ("failure") — useful when a story's ending isn't a simple success.

sections.title: New words for a real ending

items.spanish: Miután mindenki hazament, egyedül maradtam, és rájöttem, hogy ez nem kudarc volt, csak egy tanulság.
items.english: After everyone went home, I was left alone, and I realized this wasn't a failure, just a lesson.

items.spanish: Mielőtt lezártuk a napot, még megbeszéltük, mi volt a tanulság.
items.english: Before we closed out the day, we still talked over what the lesson was.

sections.content: You don't need every tool in the same sentence, and a story with a real ending rarely uses more than two or three at once — pick a sequencing connector (*miután*/*mielőtt*/*végül*) and one closing word (*eredmény*/*tanulság*/*kudarc*), and let the rest of the sentence do plain, simple work.
